3.1 Processing Seaflow data (only Gradients 1 through 5)
In this document, we will clean and bin the particle-level seaflow datasets (only Gradients 1 through 5).
This is the overall setup for binning/gridding.

title: 3  Processing Seaflow data
text:
3.2 Binning five Gradients cruises
First, we will carry out the actual binning.


Code
## Focus on the Gradients cruises
cruises = c("SCOPE_16", ## G1
            "MGL1704", ## G2
            "KM1906", ## G3
            "TN397_740", ## G4
            "TN412_130") ## G5

for(cruisename in cruises){

  ## Read particle-level data.
  vct_dir <- str_glue("{raw_data_dir}/{cruisename}/{cruisename}_vct_slim")
  vct_files <- list.files(vct_dir, "\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE)
  list_of_df = lapply(1:length(vct_files), function(ifile){ read_parquet(vct_files[ifile]) })
  vct <- bind_rows(list_of_df)
  invisible(gc())
  
  ## Do the actual gridding now
  vct["fsc_small_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["fsc_small"]],
                                           grid_bins[["fsc_small"]],
                                           labels = FALSE,
                                           right = FALSE))
  vct["pe_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["pe"]],
                                    grid_bins[["pe"]],
                                    labels = FALSE,
                                    right = FALSE))
  vct["chl_small_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["chl_small"]],
                                           grid_bins[["chl_small"]],
                                           labels = FALSE,
                                           right = FALSE))

  ## Remove beads
  vct = vct %>% filter(pop != "beads")
  
  ## Gridding the data and summing the Qcs in each 3d grid bin.
  gridded <- vct %>%
    group_by(date, across(ends_with("_coord")), pop) %>%
    summarise(Qc = sum(Qc), .groups="drop") %>%
    select(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord,  Qc) %>%
    arrange(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord)

  ## Aggregate to hourly level
  hourly_gridded <- gridded %>%
    group_by(date=floor_date(date, "1 hours"), across(ends_with("_coord"))) %>%
    summarise(Qc=sum(Qc), .groups="drop") %>%
    arrange(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord)
  invisible(gc())
  
  ## Each cruise's binned data is now saved to a file
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-gridded-before-cleaning.csv")
  outfile = file.path(outputdir, filename)
  write.csv(hourly_gridded, file = outfile, row.names = FALSE) ## TODO: write into a folder named after the cruise..
  cat("wrote to", outfile, fill=TRUE)
}


Let’s see, for every cruise, 1d plots for all 3 dimensions. This is before any cleaning.


Code
cruises = c("SCOPE_16", ## G1
            "MGL1704", ## G2
            "KM1906", ## G3
            "TN397_740", ## G4
            "TN412_130") ## G5

for(cruisename in cruises){

  ## Load data
  csv_filename = paste0(cruisename, "-gridded-before-cleaning.csv")

                            csv_filename = csv_filename)
  ylist <- datlist$ylist
  biomass_list <- datlist$biomass_list
  dates <- datlist$datetimes
  rm(datlist)
  gc()

  ## Make a 1d forward scatter (fsc) plot over time.
  plotlist = lapply(1:3, function(idim){
  datobj_1d = flowmix::collapse_3d_to_1d(ylist = ylist, countslist = biomass_list, idim = idim)
  flowtrend::plot_1d(ylist = datobj_1d$ylist,
                     countslist = datobj_1d$countslist,  bin = TRUE,
                     x = dates) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("white", "black", "yellow", "red")) +
    ggtitle(cruisename) +
    ylab(c("fsc (forward scatter)", "chl", "pe")[idim])
  })
  cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plotlist, ncol = 1) %>% print()
}

title: 3  Processing Seaflow data
text:
3.3 Data cleaning notes
Next, we will clean/process the binned data.
Here are some points that came up while cleaning data.













All binning was done using 80 bins in each direction (dimension). FSC in a given cruise usually occupies only 40-ish bins. So later, prior to fitting flowmix/flowtrend models, we should multiply the FSC bin number by 2.
Most cruises have upper CHL censoring.
G5 (TN412_130) PE values all fall in the bottom bin. Although at first glance these may look like censored points, they aren’t! We don’t and shouldn’t remove these! (They are more like truncated points.)
I’ve found that G1 has a level jump in Prochlorococcus levels in the middle of the cruise. This is apparent from 1d plots and the series of 3d bin plots.

    plot_3d_temp(ylist = newer_ylist,
                 biomass_list = newer_biomass_list,
                 tt = tt,
                 dates = dates)  
    ggsave(filename =  file.path(outputdir,
                                 paste0(cruisename, "-3d-plots"),
                                 paste0(cruisename, "-", tt, ".png")),
           width = 20, height = 7) 
  }
}


## Combine these things back into a csv-saveable table.
dates_list <- dates %>% as.list()
recombined_list <- purrr::pmap(list(dates_list, newer_ylist, newer_biomass_list), function(date_str, coords_matrix, qc_vector) {
  coords_tibble <- as_tibble(coords_matrix, .name_repair = "unique")
  colnames(coords_tibble) <- c("fsc_small_coord", "chl_small_coord", "pe_coord") # Rename columns
  coords_tibble %>%
    mutate(date = date_str, Qc = qc_vector)
})
hourly_gridded_reconstructed <- bind_rows(recombined_list) %>%
  select(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord, Qc)

## Each cruise is now saved to a file
filename = paste0(cruisename, "-gridded-after-cleaning.csv")
outfile = file.path(outputdir, filename)
write.csv(hourly_gridded_reconstructed, file = outfile, row.names = FALSE)
cat("wrote to", outfile, fill=TRUE)

4.2 2. Data Loading & Standardization
Load the cruise dataset and scale numeric features.


Code
## I think these are "plain" names
## cruisenames_plain = c("SCOPE_16", ## G1
##                 "MGL1704", ## G2
##                 "KM1906", ## G3
##                 "TN397_740", ## G4
##                 "TN412_130") %>% ## G5
##   .[2] ## Only G2 for now.


cruisenames = c("KOK1606", ## G1
                "MGL1704", ## G2
                "KM1906", ## G3
                "TN397", ## G4
                "TN412")  ## G5
##  .[1]  

for(cruisename in cruisenames){

  ## Print the markdown header for the tab
  cat_tab(cruisename)

  ## Load data
  filename = paste0( cruisename, "-X.csv")
  X <- read.csv(file = file.path(datadir, filename))%>% as_tibble()
  
  ## Extract spatiotemporal identifiers and scale numerical variables
  time0 <- lubridate::as_datetime(X$time)
  lat0 <- X %>% pull(lat)
  lon0 <- X %>% pull(lon)
  varnames <- X %>% select(-c("time", "lat", "lon")) %>% colnames()
  
  ## 1. First take the means and standard deviations
  means = X %>% select(-time, -lat, -lon) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) 
  sds = X %>% select(-time, -lat, -lon) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) 
  
  ## Base R plot
  apply(X[-c(1,2,3)], 2, mean, na.rm=TRUE) %>% sort(decreasing=TRUE) %>%
    plot(main = "Means of all variables, sorted")
  cat("\n\n") 
  
  ## 2. Then, identify which variables have really big means
  thresh = 1E10
  somenames = means[,which(means>thresh & sds > thresh)] %>% names()
  if(length(somenames) >= 1){

    ## 3. Visualize 
    p <- X[,somenames] %>%
      add_column(time = time0) %>%
      pivot_longer(-time)  %>% 
      ggplot() +
      geom_point(aes(x=time, y = value, group = name), size = .5) +
      facet_wrap(~name, scale = 'free_y')   +
      ggtitle("The unusually high-value variables")
    
    print(p)
    cat("\n\n") 
    
    ## 4. Remove these variables
    X = X %>% select(-all_of(somenames))
  }
  
  ## Store the scaling information
  scaleobj <- X %>% select(-lat, -lon, -time) %>% scale() 
  mean_val <- attr(scaleobj, "scaled:center") %>% unname()
  sd_val <- attr(scaleobj, "scaled:scale") %>% unname()
  
  ## Double check that scaling is sound
  scaled_data = as.matrix(scaleobj)
  unscaled_data <- sweep(scaled_data, 2, sd_val, `*`)
  unscaled_data <- sweep(unscaled_data, 2, mean_val, `+`)
  orig_matrix <- as.matrix(X %>% select(-time, -lat, -lon))
  
  ## Base R plot
  max_diffs <- apply(abs(unscaled_data - orig_matrix), 2, max, na.rm = TRUE) %>% sort()
  plot(max_diffs, type = "p", xlab = "Variables (Sorted)",
       ylab = "Max Absolute Difference",
       main = "Reconstruction Error per Variable")
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
  cat("\n\n") 
  
  ## Save the scaling information
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-cmap-scaling-info.RDS")
  X_scaled = scaled_data
  saveRDS(list(X_before_scaling = X,
               X_after_scaling = X_scaled,
               scaleobj = scaleobj,
               X_means = mean_val,
               X_sds = sd_val),
          file = file.path(outputdir, filename))

  ## Plot the initial scaled variables across time: 
  # X_combined <- X_scaled %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(time = time0,.before = 1)
  # scaled_plot <- X_combined %>% 
  #   pivot_longer(-time) %>% 
  #   ggplot() +
  #   geom_path(aes(x = time, y = value, group = name), alpha = 0.1, linewidth = 0.1) +
  #   theme_minimal() +
  #   ggtitle("Scaled variables over time")
  # print(scaled_plot)


  ## Analyze missingness patterns across all variables.
  ## > **Note:** Variables like salinity from GO-SHIP or GEOTRACES trajectories are naturally unavailable for non-targeted cruises ([GO-SHIP Paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01212-w), [GEOTRACES Overview](https://www.geotraces.org/cruise-overview/)).


  ## Proportion of missing time points
  num_na <- apply(X_scaled, 2, function(mycol) sum(is.na(mycol))) 
  ##print(head(sort(num_na, decreasing = TRUE)))
  
  num_time_points <- nrow(X_scaled)
  prop_missing <- num_na / num_time_points
  
  ## Missingness distribution histogram
  hist(prop_missing, breaks = 30, main = "Proportion of missing time points")
  abline(v = 0.25, col = "red", lty = 2)
  
  missing_only_few <- sum(prop_missing < 0.25)
  legend("topleft", legend = paste0("Missing only\na few:\n", missing_only_few, "\nvariables"), box.lwd = 0)
  
  missing_a_lot <- sum(prop_missing > 0.25)
  legend("topright", legend = paste0("Missing \na lot:\n", missing_a_lot, "\nvariables"), box.lwd = 0)


  ## Visualize the feature matrix before imputation (variables with $<25\%$ missing values):
  X_scaled_copy0 <- X_scaled %>% as.matrix()
  dimnames(X_scaled_copy0) <- NULL
  
  # heatmap <- X_scaled_copy0 %>% 
  #   .[, prop_missing < 0.25] %>% 
  #   drawmat_precise_ggplot() + 
  #   ggtitle("Matrix heatmap before imputation (<25% missing)")
  # print(heatmap)

  ## Matrix Completion via Low-Rank SVD (`softImpute`); we'll
  ## fill missing values using nuclear-norm regularized singular value decomposition (`softImpute`).
  X_scaled_copy <- X_scaled_copy0[, prop_missing < 0.25] 

  if(sum(is.na(X_scaled_copy)) >= 1){

    ## Fit nuclear-norm regularized SVD model
    fit <- softImpute(X_scaled_copy, rank.max = 100, lambda = 10) ## I haven't carefully chosen lambda (or rank.max); we should do this..
    
    ## Complete matrix (fill NAs using low-rank fit)
    X_hat <- complete(X_scaled_copy, fit, unscale = FALSE)

    ## Visualize the result
    # heatmap2 <- drawmat_precise_ggplot(X_hat) +
    #   ggtitle("Matrix heatmap after softImpute low-rank completion")
    # print(heatmap2)

    ## Compare imputed entries against original observed series:
    X_smaller <- X_scaled_copy
    observed_vec <- as.vector(X_smaller)
    p <- ncol(X_smaller)
    n <- nrow(X_smaller)
    
    df <- tibble(
      Time = rep(1:n, times = p),
      Series = rep(1:p, each = n),
      Value = as.vector(X_hat),
      Imputed_or_not = is.na(observed_vec)  
    )
    
    df_plot <- df %>%
      mutate(
        Series_Label = paste("Series", Series),
        Status = ifelse(Imputed_or_not, "Imputed", "Observed")
      )
    
    imputed_plot <- df_plot %>%
      group_by(Series) %>%
      filter(any(Imputed_or_not)) %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Time, y = Value)) +
      geom_line(color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_point(
        data = . %>% filter(Imputed_or_not),
        aes(color = Status),
        size = 0.3
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~ Series_Label, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c("Imputed" = "firebrick", "Observed" = "gray30")
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Time Series Imputation via softImpute",
        ##| fig-cap: "Comparison of observed vs. softImpute filled values across series"
        x = "Time Index",
        y = "Value",
        color = "Data Point"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
      )

    print(imputed_plot)

  } else {

    X_hat = X_scaled_copy0[, prop_missing < 0.25]

  }

  ## Sanity check: confirm non-imputed entries were untouched:
  (X_scaled_copy0[, prop_missing < 0.25] - X_hat) %>% 
    as.numeric() %>% 
    summary() %>%
    as.list() %>%
    as_tibble(check.names = FALSE)  %>%
    make_html_table("Summary of the reconstruction errors") %>% print()


  ## Format the imputed output, re-attach spatial coordinates, and aggregate to hourly resolution.
  varnames = colnames(X_scaled)
  remaining_names = varnames[prop_missing < 0.25]
  colnames(X_hat) <- remaining_names
  
  X_imputed <- X_hat %>% 
    as_tibble() %>% 
    add_column(time = time0, lat = lat0, lon = lon0, .before = 1)
  
  X_imputed_hourly <- X_imputed %>% 
    group_by(time = lubridate::floor_date(time, "hour")) %>%
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), mean), .groups = "drop")

  # hourly_plot <- X_imputed_hourly %>% 
  #   select(-lat, -lon) %>%
  #   pivot_longer(-time) %>%
  #   ggplot() +
  #   geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, group = name), col = "blue", alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.1) +
  #   scale_x_datetime(
  #       breaks = "1 day",
  #       labels = label_date("%b %d\n00:00") 
  #   ) +
  #   theme_minimal() +
  #   theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) +
  #   ggtitle("Hourly aggregated variables over time")
  # print(hourly_plot)

  # hourly_plot_over_lat <- X_imputed_hourly %>% 
  #   pivot_longer(-c(time, lat, lon)) %>% 
  #   ggplot(aes(x = lat, y = value, group = name)) +
  #   geom_path(col = "blue", linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.2) +
  #   theme_minimal() +
  #   ggtitle("Hourly aggregated variables plotted across latitude")
  # print(hourly_plot_over_lat)

  ## Save the imputed covariates in a single file;
  ## Saves to MGL1704-X-from-cmap-imputed-and-scaled.csv

  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-X-from-cmap-imputed-and-scaled.csv")
  write.csv(X_imputed_hourly,
            file = file.path(outputdir, filename),
            row.names = FALSE)
}

5.1 1. Environment Setup & Helper Functions
In this section, we load the necessary R packages and set up matrix visualizers.
Code
## Core tidyverse packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

## Auxiliary packages
library(broom)
library(janitor)
library(softImpute)
library(kableExtra)

#################
## Directories ##
#################

## contains files such as X-MGL1704.csv, from Dane's script
datadir = "~/Dropbox/data/ocean/seaflow-covariates" 
##datadir = "~/Downloads" 

## Output directory for the imputed hourly covariates
## outputdir = "~/repos/process-data/output/seaflow-covariates" 
outputdir = "~/Dropbox/data/ocean/seaflow-covariates" 


##############################
## Convenience functions ####
##############################
## cat_tab <- function(title, level = 3) {
##   cat(strrep("#", level), title, "\n\n")
## }
cat_tab <- function(title, level = 3) {
  # The leading "\n\n" forces a clean break from whatever printed previously
  cat("\n\n", strrep("#", level), " ", title, "\n\n", sep = "")
}

cat_image <- function(filename) {
  cat(sprintf("![](%s)\n\n", filename))
}


make_html_table <- function(mytab, table_caption = NULL) {
  mytab |>
    kable(
      format = "html", 
      digits = 2, 
      align = "c",
      caption = table_caption
    ) |>
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
}
I’ll introduce an interpolation function for sunlight, since the values are missing in several of the gradients cruises.
Specifically, I’ll fill in from the same time on the surrounding days (e.g., ±24h, ±48h).
(I’ll also linearly fill in the other covariates, for completeness.)
Code
##' Fill in missing sunlight (PAR) and covariates using multi-day offsets.
##'
##' First ensures a continuous hourly time grid, then imputes missing
##' Photosynthetically Active Radiation (\code{par}) values by averaging
##' measurements at exact multi-day offsets (with optional hourly slack), and
##' linearly interpolates other numeric columns specifically at the newly
##' imputed PAR timestamps.
##'
##' @param geodat A data frame or tibble containing a datetime column named \code{time}, 
##'   a numeric column named \code{par}, and any other relevant numeric covariates.
##' @param days Numeric. The number of days before and after to target for strict 
##'   matching (e.g., \code{days = 1} checks $\pm 24$h, \code{days = 2} checks $\pm 24$h and $\pm 48$h). 
##'   Default is `1`.
##' @param slack Numeric. The number of hours of slack (buffer window) to add and subtract 
##'   around each day offset. Default is `0` (strict exact offsets only).
##'
##' @return A tibble with a complete hourly sequence of timestamps from the minimum to 
##'   maximum time range, containing the updated \code{par_imputed} column and linearly 
##'   interpolated values for other numeric variables at the imputed PAR rows.
##'
##' @import dplyr
##' @importFrom zoo na.approx
##' @export
fill_in_par <- function(geodat, days = 1, slack = 0) {
  
  ## 0. Ensure a continuous hourly grid from the earliest to latest time
  geodat <- tibble(
    time = seq(min(geodat$time, na.rm = TRUE), 
               max(geodat$time, na.rm = TRUE), 
               by = "1 hour")
  ) %>% 
    left_join(geodat, by = "time")
  
  n <- nrow(geodat)
  
  ## 1. Generate strict hour offsets (e.g., ±24h, ±48h)
  day_offsets <- c(seq(-days, -1), seq(1, days))
  strict_hour_offsets <- day_offsets * 24
  
  ## 2. Generate slack hour offsets
  slack_hours <- seq(-slack, slack, by = 1)
  all_hour_offsets <- unlist(lapply(strict_hour_offsets, function(d_hr) {
    d_hr + slack_hours
  })) %>% unique()
  
  ## Helper to pull values at specific hour shifts for every row simultaneously
  get_offset_matrix <- function(hour_offsets) {
    sapply(hour_offsets, function(h) {
      row_indices <- seq_len(n) + h
      valid <- row_indices >= 1 & row_indices <= n
      res <- rep(NA_real_, n)
      res[valid] <- geodat$par[row_indices[valid]]
      res
    })
  }
  
  strict_mat <- get_offset_matrix(strict_hour_offsets)
  slack_mat  <- get_offset_matrix(all_hour_offsets)
  
  ## 3. Compute row means
  impute_strict <- rowMeans(strict_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  impute_strict[is.nan(impute_strict)] <- NA_real_
  
  impute_slack <- rowMeans(slack_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  impute_slack[is.nan(impute_slack)] <- NA_real_
  
  impute_val <- coalesce(impute_strict, impute_slack)
  
  ## 4. Extract the exact contributing values used for each row as a clean list-column
  ## (Pulls the row from strict_mat if available, otherwise uses slack_mat)
  contributing_list <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    if (!is.na(impute_strict[i])) {
      vals <- strict_mat[i, ]
    } else {
      vals <- slack_mat[i, ]
    }
    vals[!is.na(vals)] ## Keep only valid, non-NA contributing values
  })
  
  ## 5. Assemble final data frame
  geodat <-
    geodat %>% 
    mutate(
      contributing_values = contributing_list,
      par_imputed = coalesce(par, impute_val)
    ) %>%
    select(-contributing_values)


  ## 6. Fills in the rest of the values using linear interpolation.
  geodat = geodat %>%
    mutate(
    is_par_imputed = is.na(par) & !is.na(par_imputed),
    across(
      where(is.numeric) & !matches("time|par|par_imputed|is_par_imputed"),
      ~ {
        interpolated <- zoo::na.approx(.x, na.rm = FALSE)
        ifelse(is_par_imputed, interpolated, .x)
      }
    )
  ) %>% 
  select(-is_par_imputed)
  
  return(geodat)
}


##' Visualize Imputed vs. Original PAR
##'
##' Generates a ggplot displaying the original Photosynthetically Active 
##' Radiation (\code{par}) values alongside the newly imputed version 
##' (\code{par_imputed}) over time.
##'
##' @param geodat A data frame or tibble containing \code{time}, \code{par}, 
##'   and \code{par_imputed} columns (typically the output of \code{fill_in_par()}).
##' @param cruisename Character string. Optional name of the cruise to display 
##'   in the plot title. Default is an empty string.
##'
##' @return A \code{ggplot} object showing the overlay of original and imputed PAR.
##'
##' @import ggplot2
##' @export
make_par_plot <- function(geodat, cruisename = ""){
  par_plot <- geodat %>% 
    ggplot() +
    geom_line(aes(x=time, y=par_imputed), col = 'red', size = rel(2)) +
    geom_line(aes(x=time, y = par), col = 'black', size = rel(2)) +
      ggtitle(paste0("Imputing PAR for ", cruisename))  +
    scale_x_datetime(
      date_breaks = "1 day", 
      date_labels = "%b %d" # Format as "Month Day" (e.g., Sep 04), change to "%Y-%m-%d" if you want the year
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
  return(par_plot)
}

## Helper function for plotting matrix heatmaps
drawmat_precise_ggplot <- function(distmat, colours = c("blue", "red"),
                                   limits = NULL,
                                   xlab = "", ylab = "", title = ""){
  distmat <- as.matrix(distmat)
  longData <- reshape2::melt(distmat[nrow(distmat):1, ])

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_raster(aes(x = Var2, y = Var1, fill = value), data = longData) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = colours, guide = "colorbar", limits = limits) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title) +
    theme_minimal() + 
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1), angle = 90, vjust = 0.3),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1)),
      plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.5))
    )
  return(p)
}

## Color scale for line plots
custom_colors <- c(
    "lat"          = "black",
    "lon"          = "grey50",
    "temp"         = "#E64B35", # Warm red
    "par"          = "#F39C12", # Gold / yellow
    "salinity"     = "#2980B9", # Blue
    "conductivity" = "#8E44AD"  # Purple
)
onboard_vars = names(custom_colors)

cruises = c("SCOPE_16", ## G1
            "MGL1704", ## G2

            "TN412_130") ## G5

datlist = lapply(cruises, function(cruisename){

    file.path(raw_data_dir, cruisename, "dash", paste0(cruisename, "-geo.tsdata"))   %>%
    read.csv(sep = "\t", skip = 6)  %>% as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(time = lubridate::as_datetime(time))
  
  geodat =
    geodat %>%
    mutate(hour_group = floor_date(time, "1 hour")) %>%
    group_by(hour_group) %>%
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) mean(x, na.rm=TRUE))) %>%
    rename(time = hour_group)
  
  ## Manual adjustments
  if(cruisename == "MGL1704"){

    geodat = geodat %>%
      mutate(
          ## 1. Turn the bad value into NA
          salinity = if_else(time %in% 
                             c(lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 01:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 02:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 03:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 04:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-05-30 00:00:00")
                               ), NA_real_, salinity),
    # 2. Automatically linearly interpolating missing values based on the time vector
    salinity = zoo::na.approx(salinity, x = time, na.rm = FALSE)
    )

    geodat = geodat %>%
      mutate(
          ## 1. Turn the bad value into NA
          conductivity = if_else(time %in% 
                             c(lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 01:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 02:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 03:00:00"),
                               lubridate::as_datetime("2017-06-05 04:00:00")), NA_real_, conductivity),
    # 2. Automatically interpolate missing values based on the time vector
    conductivity = zoo::na.approx(conductivity, x = time, na.rm = FALSE)
    )

    ## Impute PAR (using exactly +/- 24 , 48, ... hours)
    geodat =
      geodat |> fill_in_par(days = 5, slack = 2) 
    geodat %>% make_par_plot(cruisename) %>% print()
    geodat = geodat %>% select(-par) %>% rename(par = par_imputed)

  }

  if(cruisename == "SCOPE_16"){
    ## Clean one single point using the average of the +-1 hours
    t_target <- lubridate::as_datetime("2016-05-02 05:00:00")
    t_prev   <- lubridate::as_datetime("2016-05-02 04:00:00")
    t_next   <- lubridate::as_datetime("2016-05-02 06:00:00")
    geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_target] <- 
      (geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_prev] + geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_next]) / 2

    ## Impute PAR (using exactly +/- 24, 48, and 72 hours)
    geodat = geodat |> fill_in_par(days = 3)
    geodat %>% make_par_plot(cruisename) %>% print()
    geodat = geodat %>% select(-par) %>% rename(par = par_imputed)
  }

  ## Manual adjustments
  if(cruisename == "KM1906"){
    geodat = geodat %>% filter(time > lubridate::as_datetime("2019-04-10 12:00:00"))  

    ## Clean one single point using the average of the +-1 hours
    t_target <- lubridate::as_datetime("2019-04-15 03:00:00")
    t_prev   <- lubridate::as_datetime("2019-04-15 02:00:00")
    t_next   <- lubridate::as_datetime("2019-04-15 04:00:00")
    geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_target] <- 
      (geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_prev] + geodat$salinity[geodat$time == t_next]) / 2

    ## Impute PAR (using exactly +/- 24 hours)
    geodat = geodat |> fill_in_par(days = 2)
    geodat %>% make_par_plot(cruisename) %>% print()
    geodat = geodat %>% select(-par) %>% rename(par = par_imputed)
  }


  if(cruisename %in% c("TN412_130", "TN397_740")){

    ## Impute PAR (using exactly +/- 24, 48, and 72 hours)
    geodat = geodat |> fill_in_par(days = 3)
    geodat %>% make_par_plot(cruisename) %>% print()
    geodat = geodat %>% select(-par) %>% rename(par = par_imputed)

  }


  return(geodat)
})

section: 5.3 Scale and save the on-board data
text:
5.3 Scale and save the on-board data


Code
for(cruisename in cruises){

  ## Take unscaled data
  X = datlist[[cruisename]]


  ## Remove some timepoints 
  if(cruisename == "MGL1704"){
    X = X %>% filter(time > lubridate::as_datetime("2017-05-28 15:00:00"))
  }

  ## Save time/lat/lon.
  time0 <- lubridate::as_datetime(X$time)
  lat0 <- X %>% pull(lat)
  lon0 <- X %>% pull(lon)

  ## Store the scaling information
  scaleobj <- X %>% select(-lat, -lon, -time) %>% scale() 
  mean_val <- attr(scaleobj, "scaled:center") %>% unname()
  sd_val <- attr(scaleobj, "scaled:scale") %>% unname()
  
  ## Double check that scaling is sound
  scaled_data = as.matrix(scaleobj)
  unscaled_data <- sweep(scaled_data, 2, sd_val, `*`)
  unscaled_data <- sweep(unscaled_data, 2, mean_val, `+`)
  orig_matrix <- as.matrix(X %>% select(-time, -lat, -lon))
  max_diffs <- apply(abs(unscaled_data - orig_matrix), 2, max, na.rm = TRUE) %>% sort()
  stopifnot(all(max_diffs < 1E-8))
  
  ## Save the scaling information
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-on-board-scaling-info.RDS")
  X_scaled = scaled_data
  saveRDS(list(X_before_scaling = X,
               X_after_scaling = X_scaled,
               scaleobj = scaleobj,
               X_means = mean_val,
               X_sds = sd_val),
          file = file.path(outputdir, filename))

  ## Save the scaled data
  X_combined <- X_scaled %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(time = time0, lat = lat0, lon = lon0, .before = 1)
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-X-on-board.csv")
  write.csv(X_combined, file = file.path(outputdir, filename), row.names = FALSE)

  ## Make a plot, just because
  scaled_plot <-
    X_combined  %>% ##%>% select(-lat) %>% select(-lon) %>% 
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & -time, ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) %>% 
    pivot_longer(-time) %>% 
    ggplot() +
    geom_path(aes(x = time, y = value, group = name, col = name), alpha = 1, linewidth = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(paste0(cruisename, ": Scaled variables over time")) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = custom_colors,
      limits = c("lat", "lon", "temp", "par", "salinity", "conductivity"),
      drop = FALSE
    )  +
    scale_x_datetime(
      date_breaks = "1 day", 
      date_labels = "%b %d" # Format as "Month Day" (e.g., Sep 04), change to "%Y-%m-%d" if you want the year
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
  print(scaled_plot)
}

5.4 Combine with CMAP-downloaded covariates


Code
cruises_cmap = c(SCOPE_16 = "KOK1606", ## G1
                 MGL1704 = "MGL1704", ## G2
                 KM1906 = "KM1906", ## G3
                 TN397_740 = "TN397", ## G4
                 TN412_130 = "TN412") ## G5

cruises = c("SCOPE_16", ## G1
            "MGL1704", ## G2
            "KM1906", ## G3
            "TN397_740", ## G4
            "TN412_130") ## G5

for(cruisename in cruises){ 

  ## Load cmap data
  cruisename_cmap = cruises_cmap[cruisename]
  filename = paste0(cruisename_cmap, "-X-from-cmap-imputed-and-scaled.csv")
  X_cmap = read.csv(file = file.path(outputdir, filename)) %>% as_tibble()

  ## Load on-board data
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-X-on-board.csv")
  X_on_board = read.csv(file = file.path(outputdir, filename)) %>% as_tibble()
  
  ## Join them
  joined = full_join(X_cmap, X_on_board, by = "time")
  
  ## Sanity check
  stopifnot(max(abs(joined$lat.x -  joined$lat.y), na.rm = TRUE) < 5E-1)
  stopifnot(max(abs(joined$lon.x -  joined$lon.y), na.rm = TRUE) < 5E-1)
  joined = joined %>% select(-lat.x, -lon.x) %>% rename(lat = lat.y, lon = lon.y)


  ## Make a final visualization of all variables (from joined), 
  ## highlighting the ones from X_on_board as black lines
  df_long <- joined %>% 
    select(-lat, -lon) %>%
    mutate(time = lubridate::as_datetime(time)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "name", values_to = "value")
  
  hourly_plot <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = time, y = value, group = name)) +
    geom_line(color = "blue", alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_line(data = filter(df_long, name %in% onboard_vars), color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 day", labels = scales::label_date("%b %d 00:00")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) +
    ggtitle(paste0("All covariates (hourly) over time: ", cruisename)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  # Optional: print or save the plot if needed
  print(hourly_plot)

  ## Make a final visualization of all variables against latitude, connected by time
  df_long <- joined %>% 
    select(-lon) %>%
    mutate(time = lubridate::as_datetime(time)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(time, lat), names_to = "name", values_to = "value") %>%
    arrange(name, time) # Crucial: ensures rows are ordered chronologically
   
  lat_plot <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = lat, y = value, group = name)) +
    geom_path(color = "blue", alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.1) + # geom_path respects time order
    geom_path(data = filter(df_long, name %in% onboard_vars), color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      x = "Latitude", 
      y = "Value", 
      title = paste0("All covariates over latitude (connected by time): ", cruisename)
    )
  
  # Print plot
  print(lat_plot)
  
  ## Save to file
  filename = paste0(cruisename, "-X-combined.csv")
  write.csv(joined, file = file.path(outputdir, filename), row.names = FALSE)
}
